basis: inputs/path_glossary_bundle.json: concept prerequisites, blocked_future_concepts and required facts
methodology: Independent needs-to-understand review, not a keyword blacklist. Exhaustive review of main and remediation text blocks, nested visual text/code, summaries, media summaries and bridges, and up-next previews. Baseline interaction sample: first check in each of 12 tiles (12/28); expanded with four hands-on classify interactions for deployment, retention, ECS task and scoped command risks (16/28 total). Reviewed sampled prompts, all options/items, feedback and hints against glossary order and supplied evidence. No generator reasoning or prior evaluator reports consulted; no deterministic gates rerun.
boundary_decisions: The two-concept tiles teach the second concept before requiring it; the first concept’s blocked list is applied to its own earlier steps, not used to reject later teaching of the second concept.
Up-next descriptions are passing previews, with no task or current explanation dependent on understanding the next concept.
A mention of lifecycle preview as a dry run does not require understanding the later automation.dry_run concept.
Flagging failed Run Command invocations requires the current per-node evidence fact, not understanding later automation.partial_failure handling.

tile_results.reason: Buildspec steps require only supplied command and artifact evidence. CodeDeploy is taught before deployment checks. Auto Scaling occurs only in the up-next preview.
Metric, warmup and bounded capacity reasoning belongs to this concept. ECR access occurs only in the up-next preview.

Publisher/consumer tests use earlier IAM foundations. Retention decisions use supplied eligibility and still-needed flags, not an understanding of later rollout or promotion mechanisms. The media bridge mentions dry run only as a name for lifecycle preview.
Listener routing, health-check correction and fail-open reasoning are taught here; no later connectivity or telemetry diagnosis is needed.
Retention-setting and expiry/deletion evidence is local to this concept. Snapshot restoration is only an up-next preview.
Source/snapshot/restored identities and marker verification are taught here. Network settings are supplied; no dependency-order restoration, RTO/RPO rehearsal or network diagnosis is required.
Reader authorization and identity-specific testing use this concept and earlier IAM foundations, not the later denied-request diagnosis workflow.
Task registration and runtime verification use supplied cluster/network settings. ECS service desired counts, rollout and task identity are not needed.
Applicable policy constraints and minimal correction/retest are taught here. Terraform saved-plan apply occurs only in the up-next preview.
Saved-plan execution and resource comparison do not require later drift reconciliation, state locking, backend configuration or replacement controls.
Per-node status/output and target-scope checks are taught here or covered by the input-target-validation prerequisite. No bounded retry, cleanup or partial-failure automation procedure is needed.
Static validation and formatting gates are taught here. Backend access is explicitly unnecessary; understanding backend configuration or state isolation/locking is not required.
